cleanIntro: The compact HK that won the largest pistol contract in U.S. law-enforcement history: short-recoil modified Browning linkless action, polygonal cold-hammer-forged barrel, exchangeable backstraps, ambidextrous slide and magazine releases, and either the LEM double-action-only trigger or a DA/SA variant with a serrated decocking button at the left rear of the frame. The P2000 shares its steel magazines with the USP Compact. Its field strip is the classic HK axle takedown with one right-side wrinkle of its own.

steps.title: P2000 or P2000SK, LEM or V3 — read your gun first
steps.action: This book covers the P2000 and the subcompact P2000SK, in 9mm and .40 S&W (and .357 SIG in the P2000's table). Identify the trigger system before touching controls: LEM variants have a bobbed no-snag hammer and no decocker; the DA/SA Variant 3 is identifiable by the serrated decocking button at the left rear of the frame beside the hammer.
steps.prose: The decocking button placement fools USP hands — it is not a lever on the side of the frame but a button you press FORWARD at the frame's rear corner. If your P2000 does not have it, there is nothing to decock: the LEM manages its own hammer.
steps.quote: On P2000 and P2000SK variants using the conventional double-action/single-action (DA/SA) mode of operation, an ambidextrous decocking button is mounted on the left, rear portion of the frame. It allows the user to safely lower the hammer from SA position to DA position. This DA/SA variant of the P2000 and P2000SK is readily identifiable by the presence of the serrated decocking button and spurred hammer.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 1 — INTRODUCTION, p.5

steps.title: It will fire with the magazine out — clear it like it means it
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger and outside the guard. The P2000 has no conventional manual safety, and except for special magazine-disconnect models it fires if a round is chambered and the trigger is pressed, magazine in or out. Clear is defined by three conditions, all required: magazine removed, slide locked rear, chamber free of brass or ammunition.
steps.prose: The book gives 'clear' a three-part definition rather than a feeling — use it as a checklist, not a vibe.
steps.quote: Clearing the Pistol - HK P2000 Series pistols are not considered “clear” or safe unless: 1. The magazine is removed from the pistol. 2. The slide is locked to the rear. 3. The chamber is free of brass or ammunition.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 1 — INTRODUCTION, p.7
steps.warn: P2000 Series pistols, except special models with a magazine disconnect, fire with the magazine removed if a round is chambered.

steps.title: Magazine out, slide locked open, watching the port
steps.action: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Then, muzzle still safe, pull the slide rearward while pressing the slide release upward and lock it open — watch for a cartridge or empty case to eject as the slide comes back.
steps.prose: Both slide releases are live on a P2000 — either side works — so lock it back with whichever thumb has the better angle.
steps.quote:
3. Open and lock slide - While pointing the pistol in a safe di­rec­tion, lock the slide open by pull­
ing the slide rearward as you press the slide release upward. Watch for a cartridge or empty case to be ejected from the pistol.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 1 — Clearing, p.7

steps.title: Chamber checked by eye and by finger
steps.action: Look into the chamber through the open ejection port, then physically insert a finger into the chamber through the port to feel for a cartridge or case, and remove anything found. Only then is the P2000 clear.
steps.prose: The finger check is not a formality: the P2000's compact port shadows the chamber mouth exactly where a rim can hide.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect chamber - Inspect chamber for the presence of a cartridge or empty case by: • Visually viewi­ng chamber through open ejec­tion port. • Physically in­sert­ing finger into chamber through ejec­tion port to check for the pres­ence of a cartridge or empty case. • Remove any cartridges or empty cases from the cham­ber or from with­in the pistol.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 1 — Clearing, p.7

steps.title: Slide to the axle recess
steps.action: Confirm the pistol is CLEAR, depress the slide release and let the slide run forward. Then with the firing hand retract and hold the slide at the point where the axle of the slide release is visible through the recess in the left side of the slide.
steps.prose: Same alignment discipline as every axle-takedown HK: the recess is the window, the axle must center in it, and your grip is what holds the position.
steps.quote: 1. Make sure the pistol is CLEAR. 2. Depress the slide release and allow the slide to move forward. 3. Using the firing hand, re­tract and hold the slide to the rear so that the axle of the slide release
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: Left release out — the right one stays put for now
steps.action: With the non-firing hand, press the axle from the right side of the frame and remove the LEFT slide release completely out of the left side. The right slide release stays attached to the frame at this stage — it comes out later, its own way.
steps.prose: The P2000's ambidextrous releases are two parts, not one through-piece — which is why this step only frees the left one and the slide.
steps.quote: 4. With the non-firing hand, completely remove the left slide release from the left side of the frame by pressing on the axle of the slide release from the right side of the frame. The right slide release will remain attached to the frame.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: Slide off, recoil assembly lifted out, barrel out
steps.action: Slide the upper forward off the frame. Lift up on the rear of the recoil spring guide rod and take the captive recoil assembly out of the slide — it is one unit and HK does not recommend taking it apart. Then lift the rear of the barrel by the locking block and withdraw it.
steps.prose: The P2000's recoil assembly carries the polymer absorber bushing of the recoil reduction system (the SK uses a double spring instead) — clean it as a unit and leave its guts alone.
steps.quote:
6. Carefully remove the recoil spring assembly from the barrel and slide by lifting up on the rear
of the recoil spring guide rod. The entire assembly can now be lifted out of the slide (see Figure 15). P2000 and P2000 SK pistols use a “captive” recoil spring assembly. Disa­ s­sem­bly of the recoil spring is not recommended. 7. Lift the rear of the barrel by the locking block and with­draw it from the slide.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: The P2000 wrinkle: right slide release out at 45 degrees
steps.action: Remove the right slide release by rotating it upward approximately 45 degrees and lifting it out of the frame. This is the step no other HK in the family has, and it is also the first thing to go back IN at reassembly — installed into its recess and rotated down until parallel with the frame's top.
steps.prose: If you forget this part exists, the pistol still field-strips — but the right release's recess is where fouling collects, and the book removes it for a reason.
steps.quote: 8. Remove the right slide release by rotating it upward approximately 45° and lifting it out of the frame.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: ⛔ No stainless steel brush in the polygonal bore
steps.action: Clean the bore with a bronze bore brush and solvent, at least six passes chamber to muzzle, then patches. The P2000's caution names stainless steel brushes specifically: they scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.prose: Polygonal bores clean easily precisely because there are no sharp corners — a bronze brush and patience beat anything harder.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Do not use a stainless steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 7 — Normal Cleaning, p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete — armorer line and the 500-round major interval
steps.action: Five pieces on the bench: slide, barrel, captive recoil assembly, frame, and the right slide release. Only an HK certified armorer goes further. Intervals: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months; Major cleaning after 500 cartridges — note, 500 on this model, not the 600 of the newer books — or when the pistol is contaminated with sand, dust or water.
steps.prose: The P2000 book's 500-round Major interval is the strictest in the current HK pistol line — hold to it rather than averaging it with its siblings.
steps.quote: NOTE: Disassembly of the pistol is now com­plete. Only an HK certified armorer should disassemble the pistol further.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — DISASSEMBLY, p.22

deepSteps.title: ⛔ US magazines only — European P2000 magazines do not fit
deepSteps.action: Before any magazine work, know the P2000's own compatibility trap: European P2000 magazines will not fit the P2000 model sold in the USA. The pistol otherwise shares steel magazines with the USP Compact.
deepSteps.prose: A magazine that will not seat is not always damaged — on this platform it may simply be the wrong continent's part, and forcing it teaches you nothing good.
deepSteps.quote: MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY NOTE: European P2000 magazines will not fit the P2000 model sold in the USA.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.24

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart — high-capacity and 10-round patterns differ
deepSteps.action: High-capacity: depress the locking detent in the floorplate with a blunt pointed instrument, hand over the base, slide the floorplate forward, ease the locking plate and spring out, remove plate, spring and follower. Ten-round: with the detent held, also squeeze the floorplate locking tabs on both sides before the parts release.
deepSteps.prose: The 10-round floorplate's side tabs are the tell — check for them before assuming the high-capacity procedure applies.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: Beware of the spring tension exerted by the mag­a­zine spring while removing and installing the mag­a­zine floorplate. Keep the base of the mag­a­zine point­ed in a safe direction (away from the face and eyes) at all times during dis­as­sem­bly and reas­semb­ ly and wear eye protection.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.24
deepSteps.warn: Base away from face and eyes, eye protection on.

deepSteps.title: Major cleaning at 500 rounds — magazine apart, parts immersed
deepSteps.action: Major cleaning is normal cleaning with the magazine disassembled and all parts rinsed with or immersed in solvent, scrubbed with a nylon brush and dried by compressed air or rag and swabs. The book allows full immersion of all P2000 parts in any solvent safe for bare hands, including ultrasonic solution.
deepSteps.prose: The immersion permission is broader than the newer HK books give — but the same ultrasonic caution applies: the colored reference markings on frame and extractor can strip, and under 10,000 rounds ultrasonic cleaning is normally unnecessary.
deepSteps.caution: Dry everything thoroughly after immersion, then lubricate before reassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Major Cleaning - Major Cleaning is the same as normal cleaning ex­cept that: • The magazine is dis­as­semb­ led for cleaning. • All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in sol­vent and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 7 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.26

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not 'improve' an HK — the alteration ban
deepSteps.action: HK's design is an optimization of safety, deployment speed, accuracy, dependability and durability, and the book bars altering any component to make the pistol 'better'. Altering any part of pistol or magazine can cause injury or death and voids the warranty.
deepSteps.prose: On the P2000 the trigger-system difference between LEM and V3 is a parts set — which is exactly why the ban matters here: the tempting swaps are real parts that really fit, and still not yours to install.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: HK pistol designs rep­re­sent an optimization of a combination of safet­y, speed of deployment, accuracy, de­penda­bil­i­ty, and durability. Do not attempt to make an HK pistol “better” by altering any of its com­po­nents. Alt­er­ing any part of the pistol or maga­ ­zine may cause injury or death and will also void any HK warranty on the prod­uct.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 7 — INSPECTION, p.27

deepSteps.title: Lubrication: light nearly everywhere, medium on the working surfaces
deepSteps.action: Use a quality medium-weight firearms oil and never a penetrating lubricant — those can deaden primers. No lube on plastic and rubber. Light lube (barely detectable to a finger) on the bore, chamber, barrel exterior, all metal parts, magazine spring, recoil assembly and sights. Medium lube (present but not running) on the barrel locking block, slide rails and grooves, operating controls, the locking insert and guiding part in the frame, and the extractor.
deepSteps.prose: The locking insert and frame guide part are the P2000-specific entries on the medium list — they are the steel the slide actually runs on, inside a polymer frame.
deepSteps.quote: Do not use lubricants that boast of their ability to pene­ trate metal as these substances may deaden prime­ rs.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 7 — LUBRICATION, p.27

deepSteps.title: After reassembly: the controls check
deepSteps.action: Once the pistol is back together, clear it and verify correct assembly and operation: the slide must move freely on the frame, and with the pistol cleared and pointed safely, every control must work — double-action mode as applicable, slide release, magazine release. On a V3 add the decocker: it must drop the hammer safely without the hammer reaching the firing pin.
deepSteps.prose: A P2000 assembled with the right slide release mis-rotated will feel fine until the release is needed — the controls check is where that gets caught, not the range.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: Assembly of the pistol is now complete. Clear the pistol and check it for correct assembly and op­er­a­tion. Be sure the slide moves freely on the frame and with the pistol cleared and pointed in a safe di­rec­tion, ensure all controls operate cor­rect­ly. As applicable, check double-action only mode, slide release, and the magazine release.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — P2000 / P2000SK — May 2026 (imprint page); published as 5.12.2026 FINAL — Section 6 — ASSEMBLY, p.23

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Nylon toothbrush moistened with solvent over all internal surfaces
Rag and cotton swabs to remove the loosened fouling

cleaning.name: BARREL AND LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Bronze bore brush with solvent, six passes chamber to muzzle — never stainless steel on the polygonal bore
Patch the bore clean, then brush the barrel exterior and locking block

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the captive recoil assembly as one unit — its absorber bushing is part of the recoil reduction system
Scrub frame carbon, concentrating on the area normally covered by the slide

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Brush the follower and feed lips at Normal cleaning
Disassemble only at Major cleaning — US-pattern magazines only
Confirm the follower runs freely and rises nearly flush against the feed lips

cleaning.name: INTERVALS
tasks: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months
Major cleaning after 500 cartridges — this book's interval, stricter than the 600 of newer HK manuals — or after sand, dust or water exposure

reassembly: Install the right slide release first: seat it in its recess on the right of the frame at about 45 degrees, engage its tab in the cutout, and rotate it down parallel to the frame top.
Position the barrel in the slide — muzzle in the front hole, locking block in the ejection port, angled locking surfaces visible along the slide's underside.

Seat the front of the recoil spring guide rod in the small hole in the front of the slide, align the rear angled surfaces with the barrel locking block's, and push forward until the retainer engages the shelf on the locking block.
Thumb the recoil assembly seated; confirm the sear axle protrudes from neither side of the frame.
Draw the slide back onto the frame so the metal inserts pick up the slide grooves.
Retract to put the left recess over the axle hole and insert the left slide release from left to right until flush.
Clear the pistol and run the controls check — slide travel, trigger mode, both slide releases, magazine release.
fncheck: Clear the P2000 and rack the slide three or four times — smooth, no binding. LEM: dry fire, hold the trigger, cycle the slide, release for the reset, fire again. V3 DA/SA: dry fire, cycle with the trigger held so the hammer stays cocked in single-action, press the decocking button — the hammer must fall to the safe position without striking the firing pin — then confirm the next pull runs the full double-action stroke. Both: an empty magazine must lock the slide open, and both slide releases and the magazine release must work from both sides.
